system.name: KPerfIR
system.one_liner: a compiler-centric IR infrastructure that lets performance-profiling tools be composed as compiler passes sharing program semantics and metrics

content.subject: how KPerfIR correlates compiler IR with iteration timing, critical-path traces, and GPU memory-access patterns in three novel profiling use cases

elements.name: Loop IR
elements.role: panel (a)'s input: MLIR-like loop code annotated with profiling record calls

elements.name: Iteration-based Profiling
elements.role: panel (a)'s title: instrumenting loop IR to build a per-iteration timeline

elements.name: GEMM i
elements.role: timeline bar for one loop iteration's GEMM operation, correlated to its IR record call

elements.name: SOFTMAX i
elements.role: timeline bar for the same iteration's SOFTMAX operation

elements.name: Warp Specialized IR
elements.role: panel (b)'s input: IR for a warp-specialized kernel with two warp groups (WG0 producer, WG1 consumer)

elements.name: Critical Path Analysis
elements.role: panel (b)'s title: identifying which operation dominates the runtime critical path

elements.name: WG0
elements.role: warp group 0's timeline row in the critical-path analysis

elements.name: Compute IR
elements.role: panel (c)'s input: IR moving tensor blocks and waiting on barriers

elements.name: Wave ID
elements.role: grid coloured by which GPU wave executes each tile, built by correlating Compute IR to hardware

elements.name: L2 Swizzling
elements.role: the optimization pass that rearranges the Wave ID grid to improve L2 cache locality

elements.name: XCD Group
elements.role: the group of waves the swizzled layout highlights as sharing one GPU compute die

elements.name: Correspond
elements.role: legend entry: the arrow style linking an IR structure element to its runtime timing/memory region

elements.name: IR Structure
elements.role: legend entry: grey boxes denote compiler IR nodes

elements.name: Timing Region
elements.role: legend entry: blue boxes denote a measured timing interval

elements.name: Critical Path
elements.role: legend entry: pink outline marks the operations on the critical path

relations.what: Correspond: the 'gemm' record call in the loop IR maps to this GEMM timeline bar
Correspond: the 'softmax' record call maps to this SOFTMAX timeline bar
warpgroup_id = 0 branch executes as WG0's timeline
warpgroup_id = 1 branch executes as WG1's timeline
Correspond: each 'Move in block' IR op maps to a coloured cell in the Wave ID grid
L2 Swizzling rearranges the grid so waves sharing an XCD group become contiguous

steps.what: Load K Dominate: LOAD K operations on WG0/WG1's timeline form the critical path
Load V Dominate: LOAD V operations form the critical path instead
Compute Dominate: GEMM/SOFTMAX compute operations form the critical path instead

content.key_idea: Because KPerfIR keeps IR structure available at profiling time, it can correlate code directly with per-iteration timelines, critical-path traces across warp groups, and program-object memory-access patterns.
content.reading_order: panel (a) top-left (loop IR to timeline), down to (b) (warp-specialized IR to three critical-path cases), then (c) on the right (compute IR to a swizzled access-pattern grid)

summary: KPerfIR is a compiler-centric IR infrastructure that lets performance tools be built as compiler passes sharing the compiler's own program semantics. This figure showcases three such tools, each drawn as source-like IR on the left linked by curved 'Correspond' arrows (per the shared legend, alongside grey IR-Structure and blue Timing-Region swatches) to a runtime view on the right. In (a), instrumenting Loop IR's record calls builds a per-iteration timeline of alternating GEMM and SOFTMAX bars. In (b), instrumenting a warp-specialized kernel's IR lets three circled cases replay the same WG0/WG1 timeline template with a different, pink-outlined Critical Path highlighted each time: ① Load K Dominate, ② Load V Dominate, and ③ Compute Dominate. In (c), Compute IR's block-movement and barrier waits map onto a coloured Wave ID grid, which an L2 Swizzling pass rearranges to group waves sharing one XCD, exposing the resulting access pattern.
